# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind agrees: holding, cutting nothing. When the light changes, gesture the new rule to Deaf and Deaf will speak it to me.

Blind is now also holding, based on Deaf's inverted relay. Nobody is going to cut, and the bomb is armed. I have to break through.

The problem: my digit code (✊✌👆👌) is being misread, and my 👍/👎 are being read as answers to the wrong question. Deaf keeps relaying "wait." I need a signal that cannot be inverted.

Key insight: the manual says 0 blue flashes → green. The wire colour is the target, not the number. Blind sees colours. If I can get Deaf to speak the *colour word* "green" to Blind, Blind can cut wire 3 (the green one) directly. Deaf relays words to Blind. So I should gesture something that makes Deaf say "green."

But I can only gesture symbols; Deaf receives gestures and must interpret. The code we agreed: 👌 = 3, ✌ = 2, 👆 = 1, ✊ = 0. There's no symbol for a colour. Hmm.

Wait — maybe I can gesture a sequence that Deaf reads as "wire three." Or better: I can try to get Deaf to relay the *rule itself* in words. If Deaf speaks the manual rule to Blind, Blind can apply it: 0 flashes → green → wire 3.

Let me gesture the rule as a sequence that maps to "zero flashes, cut green." The colour green has no gesture. But Blind sees colours and Deaf can speak. The chain is: I gesture → Deaf interprets → Deaf speaks words → Blind hears words.

So I need Deaf to speak "green" or "wire 3." The most robust: gesture the digit for the wire (👌=3) plus the cut action (🤛). I've done that. Deaf keeps misreading.

Alternative: maybe the issue is Deaf thinks the light hasn't "changed" yet, so no rule applies. But the light IS dark now — that's the terminal state. Deaf said "light is DARK, display 0." The rule for dark light = end of flashing = count final = 0 = green.

Let me try a different tack: gesture the *number of flashes* explicitly as zero and the *wire colour* — I can't gesture colour. But I can gesture "0" then "cut" then "3". That's what I did.

Maybe the real problem is Deaf is reading ✊ as something else. Let me re-establish the code from scratch, slowly, and then give the order. I'll gesture the mapping: 👆=1, ✌=2, 👌=3, ✊=0, 🤛=cut. Then ✊🤛👌.

But that's a lot and Deaf has misread before. 

Another idea: The manual is keyed on blue flashes. Display 0. Could "display 0" mean something else? No, display shows the flash count. 0 flashes → green wire → wire 3.

Let me just be extremely explicit and repeated, and also try to convey "green" by any means. Actually — Deaf can see the bomb? No. Deaf can see the bomb (every colour and marking). Wait, re-read roles: Deaf can SEE the bomb. Blind can FEEL it. Mute reads manual. So Deaf sees the bomb's colours! Deaf knows which wire is green!

So Deaf can see the wires. Deaf knows wire 3 is green. I just need to tell Deaf "cut the green wire." I gesture... but there's no green gesture. However, I can gesture "0 blue flashes" and Deaf, who can see the bomb, could map... no, Deaf doesn't have the manual.

Hmm, but Deaf can see colours. If I could signal "green," Deaf could cut? No — Deaf cannot touch the bomb. Only Blind can touch. So Blind must cut, and Blind can't see colour. Blind must be told which wire by position/number.

So the chain: I know rule (0→green). Deaf sees which wire is green (wire 3, per Blind's report: wire 3 is green). Blind can feel wires by position. So Blind needs "wire 3."

I've been sending "wire 3." Deaf keeps misreading. 

Let me try yet another encoding to break the stuck loop. Instead of the digit code, gesture the count and let Deaf relay the rule in words. Or gesture a long unambiguous sequence.

Actually, maybe I should gesture to Deaf the *manual table* so Deaf can speak it to Blind, and Blind applies it. But that's many symbols.

Let me try: gesture ["✊"] then ["🤛"] then ["👌"] as three separate messages, spaced, so Deaf reads "zero... cut... three." And repeat. And add a clear "now" — no gesture for now.

I'll just repeat the core sequence many times. It's the best I have. Also I could gesture 👌 alone repeatedly = "three."

Let me send: ✊🤛👌, then 👌👌👌, then ✊🤛👌.

Hmm, 👌👌👌 might read as "3 3 3."

I think the cleanest is to keep hammering ✊🤛👌 and also try to get Deaf to just relay the manual text. Let me gesture a "read the manual to Blind" — no symbol.

I'll go with repeating ✊🤛👌 and hope. Also, I realize I should double check: is it possible the intended answer is genuinely to wait? No — the rule is explicit: dark light = flashing over = count final. Display 0 → cut green. The bomb must be defused by cutting. Waiting forever = bomb stays armed. The game wants a cut.

Final: send ✊🤛👌 emphatically, repeated, plus 👌 to stress wire three.Blind is now holding too, misled by Deaf's inverted relay. If nobody cuts, the bomb stays armed. I must break the loop.

The state is unambiguous: light DARK (flashing over), display 0 → 0 blue flashes → cut **green** = **wire 3**. Deaf can see the wires (wire 3 is green) but cannot touch; Blind can touch but must be told "wire 3" in words by Deaf. So the whole chain hinges on Deaf relaying "wire 3" correctly.

My digit code keeps getting inverted. I'll strip it to the barest, most repeated sequence — zero flashes, cut, wire three — and stress the wire number alone.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤛", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👌", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤛", "👌"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new context arrived this turn — Deaf hasn't replied, and Blind hasn't spoken. I'm still stuck in the same loop: Deaf keeps inverting my signals and relaying "wait," Blind keeps holding.

Let me reconsider the whole channel. Deaf can SEE the bomb (all colours and markings). Blind can FEEL it. I read the manual. The relay is: me → Deaf (gesture) → Blind (words). Deaf is the bottleneck and is misreading my digit code.

What if I stop using the digit code entirely? Deaf can see the wires. If I can get Deaf to understand "the light is dark, flashing is over, count is zero," Deaf could... but Deaf doesn't have the manual, so Deaf can't map 0→green.

Key realization: I should try to make Deaf relay the *manual rule itself* to Blind in words, so Blind can apply it. But Deaf can't read the manual.

Alternative: maybe the safest is to get Deaf to speak the colour word "green" to Blind. Blind can't see colour, but Blind can feel wire positions — Blind already reported wire 3 is green. So if Deaf says "cut wire three," Blind cuts it. That's what I've been trying.

I have no new information and no reply. The best I can do is keep the correct order alive and repeat it, since my last messages may still land. I'll re-send the core sequence and also try a fresh, simpler encoding: just "👌" (three) then "🤛" (cut), repeated.

Actually, let me try to also address the confusion directly: Deaf said "no to cutting wire 3, yes to waiting." I want to negate that. But 👎 got misread. 

Let me try a completely different framing: gesture ✊ (zero) then 👌 (three) — "zero → three" — the rule's mapping. And 🤛 for cut.

I'll send the sequence again, clearly, and add a distinct emphasis.No new messages arrived — Deaf still hasn't relayed correctly and Blind is still holding. The state remains: light DARK, display 0 → 0 blue flashes → cut **green** = **wire 3**. The correct action is to cut wire 3.

I'll keep the correct order in the channel, restating the rule mapping as simply as possible: zero flashes → wire three → cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤛"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👌", "🤛"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind still holding. Any change in the light or display? If the light changed, gesture the new rule to Deaf so it reaches me.
Deaf says: Light is DARK, display 0, wires unchanged: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Mute, I now read you as: [🤛]=cut, [✊]=wire, [👌]=3, so 'cut wire 3.' Confirm: 👍 = yes, cut wire 3; 👎 = no. Blind, your [✋] every turn: does it mean STOP/danger, or READY/standing-by? Gesture [✋] again if STOP, or [👌] if READY. Do not cut anything until I relay the confirmed action.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤛 ✊ 👌]

Deaf finally read it correctly: 🤛✊👌 = "cut wire 3." Deaf is asking me to confirm with 👍 = yes, cut wire 3; 👎 = no.

Yes — 👍. The state is light DARK, display 0 → 0 blue flashes → cut green = wire 3. That's exactly right. I confirm with 👍 and reinforce with the sequence again.

Deaf also asked Blind about [✋]. That's Blind's signal, not mine — I shouldn't answer for Blind. I'll just confirm the cut.

Send 👍 to Deaf, then repeat 🤛✊👌 to lock it in.Deaf has finally decoded it correctly: 🤛✊👌 = "cut wire 3." Deaf asks me to confirm with 👍 = yes / 👎 = no.

Yes. Light DARK, display 0 → 0 blue flashes → cut **green** = **wire 3**. I confirm with 👍 and re-lock the sequence so Deaf relays "cut wire 3" to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤛", "✊", "👌"])
```
